definition: Someone reading or using a resource for their own health.
sleep_example: A college student looks up how much sleep they need.
notes: SleepLiteracy's Help Yourself is used as 'general reader': 19 of 27 Parents resources are also tagged Help Yourself. See open questions.

alt_labels: people receiving care|people living with a condition
definition: A person getting care for a health condition, using a resource about their own care.
sleep_example: Someone newly prescribed CPAP reads how to get used to the mask.
notes: Patient is a schema.org type (Person + MedicalAudience), not a MedicalAudienceType value.

definition: Someone using a resource to learn, in or out of school. Use the population tags (teens, college students) to say who they are.
sleep_example: A high-school health class unit on sleep.
notes: Role (learner) vs population (college students) split: SleepLiteracy's Students and College are both mapped to population terms too.

definition: Grouping concept for populations: the people whose health a resource is about. Combine with any role at any level (parents + teens; school leaders + teens).
notes: Grouping node. Age ranges should also be stored as numbers (schema.org suggestedMinAge/suggestedMaxAge, LRMI typicalAgeRange), not only as concepts.

definition: Babies and toddlers, birth to about 2 years.
sleep_example: Safe-sleep guidance for babies.
notes: Almost always reached through a parent or caregiver: tag the role too.

definition: Children from about 3 to 12 years.
sleep_example: A bedtime-routine chart for a 7-year-old.
notes: SleepLiteracy's term says 6-12; AASM's pediatric bands split 3-5 and 6-12.

definition: Young people from about 13 to 18 years.
sleep_example: Why teens fall asleep later, and what helps.
notes: SleepLiteracy has no 'teens' term; 'Youth' has no age range and overlaps Kids and Young Adults.

definition: Adults from about 18 to 25 years.
notes: MeSH Young Adult is 19-24 years.

definition: People enrolled in college or university, of any age.
sleep_example: Sleep and exam performance.
notes: Duplicate in SleepLiteracy: General Public > College and Universities > Students.

definition: Adults from about 18 to 64 years.
Adults 65 and older (SleepLiteracy uses 60+).
sleep_example: Sleep changes with age.
notes: Age cut-off differs: SleepLiteracy 60+, MeSH Aged 65+. Pick one and store the number.

sleep_example: Sleep across pregnancy and menopause.

definition: People who are pregnant or recently gave birth.
People in paid work, described as people (their own sleep), not as their employer.
notes: SleepLiteracy's Employees overlaps Workplace (a setting) and Municipal employees.

definition: People who work nights, early mornings or rotating shifts.
sleep_example: Sleeping after a night shift.
notes: MeSH has no person descriptor; Shift Work Schedule is the topic. SleepLiteracy's term mixes a population (shift workers) with a sector (hospitality).

definition: People employed by a city, state or national government, as people.
notes: If the content is about the city's HR rules, also tag employers-and-workplaces.

definition: People serving in the armed forces, and people who used to.
notes: SleepLiteracy's Military & Law Enforcement is mapped to the organization level instead (duty schedules).

definition: People who train or compete in sport.
sleep_example: Sleep and recovery.
notes: SleepLiteracy's term also covers coaches; coaches are mapped to teachers-and-coaches.

definition: People living with a diagnosed or suspected sleep disorder.
notes: schema.org healthCondition is the field for this.
Unused on SleepLiteracy (0 resources).
Unused on SleepLiteracy (0 resources). Culturally tailored outreach also gets community-level roles.

definition: Someone looking after a child or another person and helping with their health.
sleep_example: A parent moves the family's phones out of bedrooms at 9 pm.
notes: SleepLiteracy's two vocabularies name this differently (Parents vs Parents and Caregivers).
Safe to Sleep names grandparents as an audience.

definition: Someone caring for an adult relative or friend, e.g. a person with dementia.
People who share a home or bed with someone and affect their sleep.
sleep_example: A bed partner notices loud snoring and pauses in breathing.

definition: People someone spends time with as equals.
sleep_example: Roommates agree on quiet hours.
notes: hcf-guides#3 lists roommates, partners, friends, family and peer leaders at this level.

definition: Someone trained to help people like themselves.
sleep_example: A residence-hall peer health educator.

definition: Health professionals caring for a person one-to-one.
sleep_example: A doctor asks a patient about snoring.
notes: NCI's mammogram example puts the doctor at the interpersonal level. A clinician changing how a clinic works is acting at the institutional level: use health-care-leaders.

definition: Educators and coaches working directly with students or athletes.
sleep_example: A coach moves early practice so players can sleep.
notes: A teacher acting on school policy is at the institutional level (school-leaders). SleepLiteracy's term is misspelled ('Eductors').

definition: People coaching clients on habits outside health care.
Grouping concept: kinds of organization whose rules, schedules and culture shape health.
notes: Help Others covers levels 2 to 5; it maps to several concepts. See open questions.

sleep_example: A district moves high-school start to 8:30 am.
Dorm quiet hours; no 8 am exams.
notes: SleepLiteracy's Universities is the parent of Students and Professors, mixing institution and people.

sleep_example: Shift schedules that leave time for recovery sleep.
A clinic adds a sleep-apnea screening question to intake.

definition: Armed forces, police and other services that set duty schedules.
notes: SleepLiteracy's audience term is misspelled ('Millitary').

definition: Companies and agencies that schedule drivers, pilots and crews.
sleep_example: Fatigue rules for drivers.
notes: Driver hours are also set by regulators (public-policy level).

definition: People who set schedules, rules and services in a school or college.
sleep_example: A dean of students ends 8 am finals.
notes: hcf-guides#3 names campus wellbeing staff as an HCF reader.

definition: People who set work schedules, benefits and workplace health programs.
People who change how a clinic, hospital or health system works.
sleep_example: A nurse manager redesigns rotas to cut back-to-back nights.
notes: NIOSH's shift-work training targets nurse managers.

definition: Groups that work across organizations in a place or community.

sleep_example: A county runs an infant safe-sleep program.
notes: Also acts at the policy level when it writes local rules.

definition: People who plan and run programs for a whole community.
notes: SleepLiteracy's 'Public Health & Policymakers' is split between this and policymakers.

definition: People others in a community look to.
People who write and spread health messages for an organization or the public.
notes: hcf-guides#3 names public health communicators as an HCF reader.

definition: People who report on health or make media that shapes what people think is normal.
sleep_example: A reporter covers daylight saving time.
notes: MeSH has no 'Journalists'; these are topic descriptors.

definition: People who study health and produce the evidence others use.
notes: Level is a guess: researchers shape norms and policy but are not a level of influence themselves. See open questions.

definition: People and organizations that pay for health programs and research.
notes: hcf-guides#3 names funders as an HCF reader. Could be institutional (sets grantee rules) or policy. See open questions.

definition: Companies whose products and feeds shape habits and norms at scale.
sleep_example: An app maker adds a default bedtime wind-down.
notes: From the editors' statement summarized in hcf-guides#6. Could also sit at public-policy (as regulated parties).

definition: People who write and vote on laws and public policies, at any level of government.
sleep_example: A state legislator sponsors a school start-time bill.
notes: MeSH has no 'Legislators'; 'Policy Makers' is an entry term under Administrative Personnel.

definition: People who write and enforce rules in government agencies.
sleep_example: Hours-of-service rules for truck drivers.

definition: People and groups who campaign to pass, strengthen or defend public policies.
sleep_example: Advocates push for permanent standard time.
notes: MeSH has only Patient Advocacy; no general advocacy descriptor. Example organization: Global Health Advocacy Incubator (research/example-orgs).

definition: Organizations whose main work is changing public policy.
notes: Example: Global Health Advocacy Incubator; Start School Later (legislative work).

definition: Professional bodies when they issue position statements or lobby.
sleep_example: AASM's position on permanent standard time.
notes: Also institutional when they set practice standards for members.
NCI's wording names U.S. local, state and federal; HCF uses any jurisdiction.
